How this book is organized

The book has three parts and an apparatus.

  • Part I — The Research. What the Loagaeth is, measured: the nature of the book and its three layers (Ch. 1); the name generator, the families, the houses and the hierarchy (Ch. 2); the consonantal language and its phonology (Ch. 3); sound and voice — the book sung (Ch. 4); the signal structure, the loom (Ch. 5); the elemental arc and the geography of the book (Ch. 6). Each chapter brings the tests, the numbers, the graphs and the null models.

  • Part II — What it is NOT (Ch. 7). The honest graveyard: more than a hundred tested hypotheses that fell — the ciphers, the numerology, the astrology, the bridges to other systems (Watchtowers, governors, Sigillum, Ars Paulina, Soyga), the sacred names, the “solutions” published by others. Each refutation with its number and its null.

  • Part III — The Operative (Ch. 8). How to use the Loagaeth in ritual, derived from the measurement: pronunciation and vibration, the two voice registers, the choice of name and house, the elemental map of the work, the evocation sequence — honestly separating what is measured from what is tradition.

  • Apparatus. The numbered catalog of all findings; the methodology and the null models; the analysis modules; the glossary; the sources.

Chapter 0 — Method: the discipline of the null model

The problem of staring into chaos

A 49×49 grid of letters — 2,401 cells — repeated across nearly fifty leaves is fertile ground for pareidolia. In almost half a million letters, any name, any word, any “code” one looks for will be found, exactly as faces are found in clouds. The central problem of any honest study of the Liber Loagaeth is not to find patterns — it is to tell the real patterns from the ones chance manufactures. We call this the Babel principle: a large enough inventory accepts anything. The digits of π contain your name, mine, and every angel name ever written — that does not make them a grimoire.

Hence the single, inflexible rule of this study:

No pattern counts as real until it beats a null model.

This is not a formality. Over the course of the research, the overwhelming majority of hypotheses fell to this test — more than a hundred refutations are cataloged in Part II and the apparatus. The measurement exists to knock down beautiful ideas, not to confirm them. When one survives, it survives because it had no way to fall.

The three null models

For each claim, we build a version of the book without the structure being tested, measure the same phenomenon on it, and compare. Three nulls, from weakest to strongest:

  1. Shuffle. The same letters, in the same quantities, in random order. Preserves each letter’s frequency, destroys all order. It is the base null: if the real phenomenon does not beat the shuffle, it is pure effect of the letter composition.

  2. Markov-3 surrogate. A text generated letter by letter respecting the three-letter transition probabilities of the real book. Preserves the local habits of writing (the common pairs and triples). A pattern that beats the shuffle but not the Markov-3 is merely a by-product of the phonotactics — not an independent signal. This null is the hardest, and several “sound” findings (Ch. 4) shrink before it; we say so, rather than hide it.

  3. Controlled permutation / anagram. For positional and directional tests, only the relevant units are shuffled (the rows of a face, the order of the leaves, the digits of a number), preserving the rest. Isolates the specific effect.

The ruler: the z-score

A finding’s strength is the z-score: how many standard deviations the real value lies above (or below) the null distribution.

z-score reading
|z| < 2 within chance. Does not count.
|z| ≈ 2–3 suggestive, fragile. Reported as a lead, not a finding.
|z| > 3 real. Survives the null.
|z| > 6 decisive.

A strong negative z is also information: it means the real value is below chance — an anti-structure. (Real example: along the line, identical letters avoid each other; immediate repetition has z ≈ −4.5, [a75].)

Conventions and honesty

  • Fixed seed (1583). All randomness uses the same seed — the year of Dee’s first reception of the Book — so that every test is reproducible bit by bit.
  • Standard-library Python. No external dependencies in the analysis: anyone can run the modules (src/aNNN_*.py, python src/run_all.py) and get the same numbers. Each module writes a results/*.json with its statistic.
  • Explicit verdict. Each finding is marked REAL (beat the null), REFUTED (fell), LEAD (fragile) or DESCRIPTIVE (a fact true by construction or inspection, with no claim of hidden signal).
  • What failed is reported as loudly as what passed. A cherished hypothesis that falls is a result, not an embarrassment. Part II of this book exists for that.
  • Separation of planes. The measurement answers “is there objective structure?”. It does not answer “does it work as magic?” — a question of another plane, the operative one, which Part III treats in its own logic. A REFUTED verdict means “there is no objective cipher here”, not “it does not work as practice”.

The data

The source is the transcription of the 48 leaves of the Liber Loagaeth (Sloane MS 3189), each leaf with two sides (“a” and “b”), most of them dense 49×49 grids; leaf 1 is spaced into words (it is the lexicon page); the 49th leaf “that is not, was not, and shall not be known” exists only by report. The reference transcription is Clay Holden / Joseph Peterson’s; we checked an independent transcription (kondor.de) and it is a copy of Peterson’s — it differs by 1 letter in 23,712 [a53], which closes the door on source errors.

The alphabet is the 21-letter Enochian: A B C D E F G H I L M N O P Q R S T U X Z (no J, K, V, W, Y). The comparison corpus — Calls (Claves Angelicae), Watchtowers, 91 governors, Heptarchy, gematria — comes from the reference editions (Sloane 3191, A True and Faithful Relation, Liber Scientiae).

With the method in place, let us turn to what the measurement revealed.

PART I — THE RESEARCH

Chapter 1 — What the Liber Loagaeth is

Not noise, not a cipher: a language

The first question is also the most basic: what are these grids? Noise? A cipher? A text in some language? The measurement answers with convergent evidence that it is a language — constructed, strange, but a language — and not noise nor a hidden code. Four independent measures establish it.

Zipf’s law

In every natural language, word frequency falls along a power law with a slope near −1. Measured on the Loagaeth — taking the recurrent names as “words” — the Zipf slope is −1.31 with an r² fit of 0.96 [128_zipf, a92]. This is language behavior, not a random sequence (which would give a slope near zero). And more: the real book has 88 distinct names in its recurrent inventory, against 68.8 in a surrogate of the same size — the book is richer in vocabulary than its own phonotactic noise.

Entropy and memory

The mean uncertainty per letter, measured as compressibility, decisively separates the book from chance. Compressed, the real text spends 3.55 bits per letter (zlib) or 3.28 (bz2); the same text shuffled spends 4.58 and 4.32. The difference — about a full bit per letter — is real structure: there is memory, there is rule, the letters are not drawn at random [19_machine, section C].

Where does that memory come from? From a very specific ruler. Measuring a letter’s uncertainty given its context: alone, a letter carries 3.95 bits; knowing the letter above (the column), it drops to 3.94 — almost nothing; knowing the letter to the left (the line), it plunges to 3.09 [19_machine, section B]. The book’s memory is horizontal. We keep this fact: it is the reading key for all of Chapter 3 and Chapter 5.

Morphology

The names show a Semitic-type structure: a consonantal root clothed in a vowel pattern. The cleanest proof are the minimal pairs — names identical except for one vowel — exactly like the pola/pala Dee himself recorded: 13 of them, far above chance, while pairs differing by a consonant are rare (only 2) [a92, #358, #403]. Identity is in the consonant; the vowel is swappable. Chapter 2 dissects this generator.

The line as inventory

A fourth signal, independent and strong: each 49-letter line is a balanced inventory of the alphabet. The letters spread evenly across the 49 lines of a face far more than chance allows — the consonants at density 0.71× the expected (z ≈ −4.5), and the effect appears in 36 of 42 leaves tested; no null reproduces it [a75]. The line is not a sentence: it is a deliberate distribution, almost a verse built to “contain a bit of everything”.

What the book says of itself, in the diaries, matches the measure: “every letter here bringeth furth the Names of God: but they are but one Name” — every letter brings forth the Names of God, but they are one Name. And: “49 voices, whereunto the so many powers shall be obedient.” A book of names and of voices.

Three layers

The measurement separates the book into three distinct strata, each with its own statistical signature:

Leaf 1 — the language. The only leaf spaced into words, it is the lexicon: real recurrence, well-formedness, word families, prosody marked with stress accents. Leaf 1 shares fine vocabulary with the Calls: reading the grid every way, 489 Call words reappear, and Call 1 finds 68 of its 86 words [a94, a98]. It is the sister-page of the Claves [#331, #333].

Leaves 2–48 — the name field. The dense grids. They are not sentences: letter order carries no sentence information (no sentence syntax survives the null — broad word order gives 19 ordered pairs against 16.2 in the surrogate, [a106]). They are a generated field of names recurring in families. One enters through leaf 2 — leaf 1 is sealed, with no Key.

The seam 26–28 — the threshold. An anomalous band where straight reading fails and content passes to the diagonal. It is the zone of highest entropy and lowest compressibility in the whole book (Ch. 5): the point of maximum disorder, the threshold. It is also the densest in names when read diagonally (44 per thousand letters against 29 straight), which validates the diagonal reading there [a96].

The arc of the book: density and dissolution

Mapping name density leaf by leaf, the book has shape: it opens, thickens at its middle, and dissolves at its depth. The “deep” (leaves 41–48) is dissolution: the names vanish, repetition collapses, entropy rises, the vowel darkens from A to U [#360, #382].

This arc is one of the book’s most robust findings, because three independent measures point to the same dissolution zone in the deep — the vanishing of names [#360], the darkening of the A→U vowel [#382], and the fracture of elemental identity [#397]. The book’s end unravels along every measurable dimension. It is all of Chapter 6.

What the book does NOT claim to be

A piece of honesty that governs all the rest: we measured a language skeleton and a partial dictionary. The full meaning of each name — what NOCHA “means” — is either in the few anchors translated from the Calls, or it belongs to the practice, not to the page. The Call words have translations placed in position by Dee; our root-names (NOCHA and company) have zero translation anchor [a97]. Dee’s own record is explicit: “Interpret not.” There is no hidden translation to decrypt. This is not a gap in the study; it is a finding, confirmed from within (no internal cipher survives the null — Part II) and from without (no source gives a gloss).

What there is is the anatomy of the language. That is what the next chapters dissect.

Chapter 2 — The name generator

If the Liber Loagaeth is a field of names, the next question is mechanical: how are those names made? The measurement shows they are neither drawn letter by letter nor copied from a list — they are generated by a small set of rules that assemble each name from pieces. This chapter dissects those pieces, the families they form, the two houses that govern the assembly, and the hierarchy that emerges from frequency.

Prefix · root · suffix

The Loagaeth’s names decompose, for the most part, into a three-slot mold:

[prefix] · [root] · [suffix]

The root is the consonantal heart — the name’s identity (Ch. 3). The prefix and suffix come from a small, recurring inventory. Real examples, from the generative grammar [a81]:

Form Decomposition
AD-NOCHA prefix AD- · root NOCHA
NOCHA-P root NOCHA · suffix -P
I-CHASTOR prefix I- · root CHASTOR
AL-GETH prefix AL- · root GETH

This is the signature of a morphological generator: few edge pieces, many roots, ruled combination. A shuffled text does not produce recurring affixes aligned to word edges — the Loagaeth does [#334].

The grammar is predictive

The proof that the generator is real, not a description we imposed on chaos: it predicts names that exist. Combining known roots and affixes to generate forms we had not yet cataloged, 32 new names actually appeared in the book, above chance [a82]. The space is finite — about 1,320 combinations of depth 1. A grammar that generates verifiable forms is a grammar, not an illusion. [CONFIRMED NEW]

The name families

Related roots form families — sets of names sharing a consonantal skeleton. The study isolated the main ones, each with its measured reach:

Family Occurrences Leaves Role
NOCHA 447 ~35 the king-name; matrix of the D-/AD- house
GETH / ALGETH 359 — the rival house, L-/X- prefixes
CHASTOR 184 35 the spine, with nested titles
ANZACH 153 39 body, twin of HANZACH
HANZACH 76 33 H- variant
ACLAXT 76 15 zonal (Air)
ALGETHA 62 26 deep
DAXVAR 41 17 opening

The families are not imposed by the analyst: they emerge from a clustering by edit distance and survive the null [#336]. And each name is woven into the grid: the exact order of its letters traces a path (king-move) far above its own shuffled letters — 232 of 460 measured pairs are “woven”, and CHASTOR appears woven in 30 of 37 leaves [a77]. The name is not resting on the grid; it is stitched into it.

The hierarchy by repetition

Frequency draws a clean hierarchy [a80]:

NOCHA (447×) › ADNOCHA › NACHO › CHASTOR › ANZACH › … › singletons

The most repeated name has the greatest reach; the names appearing only once (singletons) are the base of the pyramid. In an operative reading (Part III), this suggests kings (the very repeated, house matrices) and lesser angels (the singletons) — but the measure guarantees only frequency, not an org chart; the hierarchy is constructive, not a proven protocol.

The two houses

Above the families lies a deeper division: two grammatical houses, distinguished by the behavior of the affixes [#405]:

House NOCHA House GETH
Dominant prefixes D- (31×), AD- (19×) A- (21×), L- (13×), X-, R-
Register vowel lighter (A/O) darker
Territory middle and body edges and deep

D- and AD- mark the NOCHA house (DNOCHA, ADNOCHA — nearly all the ~50 occurrences are NOCHA); L-, X-, R- mark the GETH house (ALGETH, ACLAX). It is not free combination: the preferred affix depends on the root’s house — a rudimentary system of classes/declension, like grammatical gender. It is the generator’s most robust grammatical fact: the book declines its names by house. [#405, corrects #335]

Super-names: chains of two roots

Some long names contain smaller names, and some are chains of two roots — fusions of houses [a99, a100]:

  • CHASTORACHANZA (3×) = CHASTOR + ACHANZA
  • GETHALCHADAX (3×) = GETH + ALCHADAX

These fusions appear about 5.5× above the surrogate — deliberate, not chance collisions. And there is a first sign of syntax between names: the compound GETHACLAX occurs 17 times in the order GETH→ACLAX and zero in the reverse (26× above chance); GETHACLAXTO appears 6× against 0.25 expected [a101, #141]. GETH is lead-root. It is the only pair with proven fixed order — broad word syntax was refuted (Part II), but this real pair exists.

Minimal pairs: the proof of the vowel

The cleanest evidence of a morphological generator are the minimal pairs. Dee himself recorded pola / pala. The measurement finds 13 pairs differing only by one vowel, against only 2 differing by a consonant — and those 2 respect phonological class (DNOCHA/DNOPHA, stops; ADNACH/ADMACH, nasals) [#358, #403]. A vocalic minimal pair can only exist if the consonant is the identity and the vowel is a swappable piece.

Two layers of lexicon

Finally, the names organize into two layers [a84]:

  • a substrate of short, omnipresent roots (the common material);
  • a deliberate layer of long compounds, placed above chance (the built names).

The Loagaeth is, in sum, a generative onomasticon: a book made to generate names of forces, with a fixed alphabet, Semitic-type morphology (root + vowel + affix), a lexicon in families and houses, root chains and a sign of syntax. The generator is morphological, not arithmetical — there is no encoded number, date or coordinate (Part II refutes it item by item). It assembles sounds with identity, not ciphers.

Chapter 3 — The language: consonant, register, phonology

Chapter 1 showed that the Loagaeth is a language; Chapter 2, how it assembles names. This chapter dissects the language from within: where identity lives, what the vowel does, why the consonant system is that of a natural language, and why it all reads along the line.

Identity is consonantal

The central structural discovery: the consonant carries identity; the vowel carries register. It is the principle of the Semitic languages, where the root is a skeleton of consonants and the vowels that clothe it give the concrete word.

The proof is the entropy by class [#402]. The consonant is nearly unpredictable (carries almost all the information); the vowel is predictable, from a small set, and in the names it collapses into A:

Register Vowel entropy Consonant entropy
Names (invocation) 1.25 bits 3.48 bits (of 3.81 max)
Calls (speech) 1.96 bits 3.91 bits (of 4.17)
Book (whole) 1.80 bits 3.81 bits

In the names, the vowel holds only 1.25 bits — almost no lexical information — while the consonant saturates near the maximum. The consonant is the word; the vowel is the melody that carries it.

The minimal pairs (Ch. 2) confirm case by case: swapping the vowel does not create another identity — it creates another form of the same name. The operative implication, kept for Part III: the name is recognized by its consonants; the vowel is freedom of register.

The consonant system is a natural phonology

The Loagaeth’s consonants are not a pileup: they form a balanced phonological inventory, like a natural language’s [#403].

  • Place of articulation: coronal 53%, velar 21%, labial 15%, glottal 11%. Coronal dominance is the unmarked place, typical of natural languages.
  • Manner of articulation: stop 35%, fricative 29%, liquid 18%, nasal 17% — entropy 1.93 of 2.0 max, the four manners well represented. A balanced inventory, not a biased noise.

This phonological coherence raises the confidence that it is a designed language, not random: chance does not produce a consonant system balanced in place and manner.

The vowel is register

If the vowel is not identity, what is it? Register — the “tone” in which the name is uttered. The vowel distribution changes from region to region, darkening from A (open, bright) to U (closed, dark) toward the deep (Ch. 6). The vowel is the parameter the book modulates while keeping the consonants as anchor. It is the melodic layer — what, in Ch. 4, turns out to be literally singable.

The phonotactic laws

A language has phonotactics — rules of what may follow what. The Loagaeth’s are those of a balanced, pronounceable language:

  • No-doubling rule. Identical letters avoid sequence: immediate repetition is far rarer than chance (anti-structure, z ≈ −4.5). A language made to be spoken avoids the stumble of gemination.
  • Marked line edges. The line’s start prefers a consonant; its end, a vowel. Words do not spill arbitrarily across the edges; there is a template [#42, #391].
  • C(C)-V syllable. Vowels almost always appear alone in the nucleus (run = 1); consonants in groups averaging 1.94. The syllabic beat is consonant(s)-vowel [#400].

The grammar is horizontal only

The decisive test of direction measures the mutual information (how much one letter predicts its neighbor) on each axis [#400]:

Direction Mutual information
Horizontal (→) 0.60 bits
Vertical (↓) 0.007 bits
Diagonal (↘) 0.016 bits
Anti-diagonal (↙) 0.008 bits

The grammar is ~90× stronger in the horizontal. The columns and diagonals have no syntax — what they hold is template (a mold of form, not of meaning; Ch. 5). This settles the reading question: the Loagaeth is read along the line, left to right — except the seam 26–28, where content locally migrates to the diagonal, a local trick, not a grammatical direction.

The same conclusion comes from the 2-D rule (Ch. 1): knowing the letter above (vertical) barely reduces uncertainty (3.95 → 3.94 bits), but knowing the one to the left (horizontal) reduces it greatly (3.95 → 3.09) [19_machine].

The grammar’s horizon: short

How far does the rule reach? Memory exceeds chance only at distances of 4 to 12 letters; beyond that, it is only side-to-side mixing [a22, #74]. The Loagaeth’s grammar is short-range — local rules for assembling syllable and name, not long periods of sentence syntax. One more proof that these are names, not sentences: a name is a short, closed unit; a sentence chains long dependencies. The Loagaeth has none.

A single direction

Final proof that the language has one direction: read backwards (mirrored), it falls apart — CHASTOR, which appears 179 times read forward, appears zero times reversed; the forward letter model spends 3.5 bits, the reversed 6.1 [a21, #67]. The text has a front and a back; only the front carries names.

Synthesis

The Loagaeth’s language is: consonantal in identity, vocalic in register, phonologically balanced, horizontal, short-range and single-direction. It is a language designed to name and to be uttered — not to narrate and not to hide. The next chapter carries this to its consequence: the book was made to be sung.

Chapter 4 — Sound and voice: the book sung

This chapter gathers the finding that brings the analysis closest to practice: the Liber Loagaeth is not merely pronounceable — it is made for the voice. The diary itself calls it “Speech from God”, to be spoken; leaf 1 bears stress accents. The whole study treated the book as text; this axis tested the vocalization. Five real signals support it — and one honest caveat limits them.

The five signals of the sound axis

Each property was measured against a random null (same frequency and length). All passed [a217–a223]:

Property Real Null z Entry
Pronounceable (C-V alternation) 0.71 0.46 +6.9 #386
Well-formed syllable (no stop-stop) 1.00 0.95 +3.2 #386
Assonance (vowels between neighbors) 0.706 0.673 +5.1 #387
Final vowel (open syllable) 60% 36% +3.2 #391
Vowel melody (top-5 skeletons) 78% 45% +5.2 #392
A-pulse every ~3 letters — — +31.5 #398

The honest caveat

Against the strongest null — the Markov-3 surrogate — the pronounceability signal shrinks (z ≈ 1.5–1.9) [#386]. This does not knock the finding down; it localizes it: cantability is not exclusive to the names, it is embedded in the book’s own letter grammar as a whole. The book is singable throughout, not just in the names. We say this instead of hiding it — the difference between a finding and an advertisement.

And two sub-hypotheses fell, honestly:

  • Chosen meter: the names have 2–3 syllables, but the concentration on a syllable count does not beat chance (z = +0.49). The lines are nearly isosyllabic (~17.6 syllables, deviation ~1.0; figure 4.2), but that is an effect of the fixed line length, not a chosen poetic meter [#386, 63_metre].
  • Rhyme: the same final vowel between neighbors gives z = +0.74 — not special [#387]. The book is metrical and assonant, but not rhymed.

The prosody is Latin

Dee was a Latinist, and he marked the angelic words with Latin prosody. Of the 676 stressed words on leaf 1, the stress falls [#388]:

  • penultimate (paroxytone): 52%
  • antepenultimate: 31%
  • final (oxytone): 15%
  • fourth syllable or beyond: 0%

83% within the window of the last three syllables, zero outside it — exactly the Latin stress rule of liturgical Latin, with penultimate dominance. Real examples: alídes, orcánor, onédon, gamésad. The stress mark tells how to recite: penultimate cadence, from church Latin.

The melody is on A

The most common vowel skeletons — AA (17), OA (5), AOA (4), AE (3), AO (2) — cover 78% of the names. The vowels barely vary; they concentrate on A. It is the model of the mantra: fixed vowel (the sustained note), variable consonant (the articulation). The Loagaeth is intoned on A [#392].

And it closes on a vowel or on an aspirated H: of the 1,258 H on leaf 1, 59% are word-final (chance would give ~25%) [#394]. Words end in tone (sustained vowel) or breath (H), rarely in a hard consonant. It is the closing rule of a sung idiom.

Two voice registers

A finding that unifies the Enochian corpus: the Calls and the table-names are the same language, in two voice registers [#401, #402].

Calls (full speech) Names (invocation)
Phonotactics identical (C-V 0.69 vs 0.68) identical
Ends in a vowel 31% 60%
A among the vowels 38% 71%
Vowels used balanced A/I/O only A

The phonotactics are identical — it is one language. What changes is the vocalic layer: the Calls are full speech (balanced vowels, consonantal ending, prose); the names are the invocation register (vowel reduced to A, open ending, sustained). This explains why the Loagaeth reads as names and not as sentences: it is the same language reduced to a name-of-power. One speaks the Call; one sings the name.

Pronunciation, in practice

The measurement delivers pronunciation rules, and Dee’s letter-names allow vibration (spelling by each letter’s name) [#395]:

Letter Name (Dee) Sound
A Un open “ah”
N Drux “n”
O Med “oh”
H Na aspirated/breath
R Don rolled “r”

So NOCHA vibrates as Drux·Med·Veh·Na·Un. The rules of the chant:

  1. Open syllables — say each letter, do not swallow vowels.
  2. Lean on the A — the projection note; where there is a strong A, the voice rises and vibrates.
  3. End on the vowel (or H) — sustain the tone, or release the breath.
  4. Penultimate stress — the Latin cadence.
  5. Pulse every ~3 letters — the A-beat governs the tempo.
  6. Descend the tessitura — bright (A) in the body, dark (U) in the deep.

Chapter 8 turns these rules into a ritual sequence. First, the next two chapters close Part I: the signal structure (the loom) and the elemental arc.

Chapter 5 — The signal structure: the loom

The language runs along the horizontal (Ch. 3). But the grid has two dimensions, and the vertical is not empty — it carries form, not meaning. This chapter separates the two and describes the book’s physical architecture: the loom on which the names are woven.

Two opposite signatures: anti-repetition and template

The structure has two signal effects of opposite signs, each on its own axis:

  • Horizontal: anti-repetition. Along the line, identical letters and short patterns avoid each other below chance (strong negative z). The line flees repetition — the behavior of a text that advances, that does not step on the same place [#369a].

  • Vertical: template. The column, by contrast, has repetition — the columns follow a pattern that reasserts itself leaf after leaf (the modular column effects give z of 8.7 to 35 under the right lens, but they are mold structure, not message: vertical mutual information is only 0.007 bits) [#398, #400].

The contrast is the reading key: information travels along the line; form is sustained by the column. The book is a loom — the horizontal weft (the names) runs over a vertical warp (the template) that holds it in place. This is why no vertical reading finds names (Part II): the column was never made to be read, it was made to hold.

The seam 26–28: the threshold

In the band of leaves 26 to 28, straight reading fails and content migrates to the diagonal. That seam is, by three independent measures:

  • the zone of highest entropy in the book;
  • the zone of lowest compressibility — nearly incompressible, close to random (z ≈ −1, against z = −165 in the middle) [#399];
  • the point where the reading direction turns, and where diagonal name density spikes (44 per thousand vs 29 straight) [a96].

It is the book’s threshold — the central fold where order undoes itself before forming again. In an operative reading (Part III), the seam is the threshold: the point of passage, of maximum chaos, between the upper and lower halves.

The four bands and their borders

The book’s face divides into horizontal segments with distinct statistical profiles — not a uniform block. The measured borders between segments are sharp [27_doubts]:

Border Between leaves
opening | middle 5b | 6a
middle | seam 25b | 26a
seam | diamonds 28b | 29a
diamonds | end 43b | 44a

Each segment has its own name density and register. It is the book’s internal architecture: rooms with marked doors, not a smooth whole.

The geometry of the diamonds: a single path

Parts of the book (leaves 29–43) organize into diamonds — stepped pyramids of letters that grow to a wide line and shrink back. We tested whether there are many reading paths within a diamond or a single one: a single path survives the null [a29]. The diamond is not a maze of possible readings; it has one correct reading trail, the others are noise. The a/b sides of a diamond are not two distinct vocabularies (Jaccard 0.279 vs 0.277 in the split — refuted) — they are the same language [#103].

Islands of order

Mapping compressibility leaf by leaf, the book is neither uniformly ordered nor chaotic: it has islands of order. All leaves compress better than shuffled (z of −33 to −165 = real structure), but the order concentrates in the body (leaves 11–22; leaf 21 is the most ordered of all, z = −165), and the chaos peaks at the seam 26–28 [#399]. The book’s order has relief: valleys and mountains, not a plain.

Grammatical dialects by region

The book is not a uniform language: it has dialects by region. Measuring internal perplexity (how well each region predicts itself, order-3 model): body 2.47, seam 3.32, deep 2.93 [#400]. Each region predicts itself better than it predicts the others — there are grammatical accents, and the seam is the most irregular (confirming the threshold’s chaos).

The leaf order is deliberate

Finally: the sequence in which Dee laid out the leaves is not arbitrary. Neighboring leaves are more alike than random leaves — there is a gradient the ordering respects (the density and vowel arc of Ch. 6). On the 7×7 plane, neighbors are more similar (0.59 vs 0.37), but that comes from the book’s smooth order, not from a magical plane geometry [a103]. The book was sequenced, not stacked at random.

Synthesis

The Loagaeth’s physical structure: a line that advances (anti-repetition), a column that sustains (template), a single-path diamond, four bands with marked borders, islands of order in relief, dialects by region, a threshold-seam at the center, and a deliberate leaf order. It is an object built with architectural care — a loom, not a heap. Over that loom runs the language; under it, the mold holds it.

Chapter 6 — The elemental arc: density, dissolution and function

Closing Part I: the book has an arc — a shape that runs from start to end and changes character along the way. Three independent measures draw the same arc, which is why it is one of the most robust findings of the whole study. This chapter also faces the elemental question head-on, with the honesty it demands — including the correction the reader-researcher himself imposed on the study.

The arc: it opens, thickens, dissolves

Mapping the book leaf by leaf, one sees a three-beat shape:

  1. Body (leaves ~2–40): density and order. Name density rises and peaks at the middle. It is the region of islands of order (Ch. 5), where structure tightens and names recur in families. Here the book is full.

  2. Seam (26–28): the threshold. At the center, the chaos peak (Ch. 5): maximum entropy, minimum compression, the reading turns to the diagonal. The book’s fold.

  3. Deep (leaves ~41–48): dissolution. At the bottom, everything undoes itself: the names vanish, repetition collapses, entropy rises, the vowel darkens from A to U. The book dissolves at its end [#360, #382].

The finding’s strength is the convergence: three measurable, independent dimensions — the vanishing of names [#360], the darkening of the vowel [#382], and the fracture of elemental identity [#397] — point to the same dissolution zone in the deep. When three different rulers agree, it is not an artifact of one of them; it is a real property of the object.

The zonal heat map

Within the body, the families have a preferred address — not rigid borders (revised to moderate), but a real zonal gradient [a78]:

Zone of the book Dominant family
Opening CHADAX / DAXVAR
Front/middle house NOCHA, ACLAXT (Air)
Spine CHASTOR
Bottom/deep house GETH, CHIDNO, ALGETH

The families migrate along the book. This map comes out by two independent methods — the king-move weave and the straight reading — and both give the same map [a78]. To walk the Loagaeth leaf by leaf is to cross territories of names that succeed one another.

The elemental question, with full honesty

Tradition links regions of the Loagaeth to elements. The study tested this rigorously — and here full honesty is required, because the elemental systems conflict with each other, and because the study erred once and had to correct itself.

There are two classic (Golden Dawn) ways to assign an element to an astrological position, and they disagree in the deep:

  • By sign triplicity (the element of the house’s zodiac sign);
  • By planetary ruler (the element of the planet ruling the house).

The correction

In a first version [#395], the study used only the sign system (which gives Earth→Water) and presented it as settled — hiding the Fire that earlier maps noted. The reader-researcher caught the error: “if everything is Earth, why had I said Air and Fire at the end?”. The audit [#396] corrected it: there are two systems, they conflict by design, and the element can only be fixed where the two agree.

The honest result

Measuring the book by both rulers, leaf by leaf [#397]:

Region By sign By planet Verdict
Body (leaves 1–40) Earth Earth Agree → Earth (robust)
Deep (38, 40, 41–48) Water Fire Conflict (water/fire 7, water/earth 3)

38 of 48 leaves have sign = planet — firm elemental identity. The 10 in conflict are all at the end [38, 40, 41–48]. The body of the book is, by both measures, Earth — matter, body, the concrete. But the deep is ambiguous: by sign it is Water; by planet it is Fire.

This is not a failure of the measurement — it is the very signature of the dissolution. In the deep, where names vanish and the vowel darkens, the elemental identity also fractures: the book reaches a region where the correspondence system itself ceases to give a single answer. The dissolution is total — it reaches even the element. It is the alchemical solve in two ways: dissolve (Water) or consume (Fire).

The method lesson: never present one attribution system as “the” element — they diverge by design, and only where they agree (body = Earth) is it firm.

The element of the letters

Below the astrology of the houses lies a simpler layer: each letter has an element assigned by the Enochian alphabet. The map [181_atlas]:

  • Earth: A, E
  • Air: H, M, O
  • Fire: C, G, I
  • Water: L, N, P

Since the dominant vowel is A (Earth) and the articulating consonants include N (Water), the elemental tension is embedded in the phonology itself. (The phrase “body-Earth / voice-Air” from an earlier version was too loose — the voice/body attribution depends on the system, and was corrected [#397].)

Function by region (operative summary)

Gathering the arc, the zonal map and the element, the Loagaeth has a function that changes by region — the basis of ritual use (Part III):

  • Leaf 1 — sealed lexicon. The language itself; one does not “enter” by it. Source, not door.
  • Opening and body (2–40) — Earth, dense names. The region of identity and presence: numerous, recurrent, stable names. From here the beings are called.
  • Seam (26–28) — the threshold. Threshold, passage, maximum chaos. Turning point.
  • Deep (41–48) — dissolution, fractured element. Zone of undoing and crossing — Water or Fire, per ruler and intent. Not stable identity.

Close of Part I

Part I measured the whole Loagaeth: it is a language (Ch. 1), with a generator of names, families, houses and hierarchy (Ch. 2), consonantal and phonologically coherent (Ch. 3), singable on A with Latin prosody (Ch. 4), woven on a loom of line-and-column with dialects and islands of order (Ch. 5), with an arc that opens, thickens and dissolves, and a function that changes by region (Ch. 6). All measured, all against the null. Part II buries what did not survive; Part III uses what did.

PART II — WHAT THE LIBER LOAGAETH IS NOT

Chapter 7 — The graveyard: everything that fell, and why

This is the part of the book that most sets it apart from anything else written on the Loagaeth. The esoteric tradition accumulates claims; this study tests them, and reports the ones that died as prominently as the ones that lived. Each refutation below has its number and its null model. The Babel principle (Ch. 0) guarantees that something is always found in half a million letters — so only what beats chance counts, and here is what did not.

7.1 The ciphers and codes

# Hypothesis Measure Verdict
7 Mirrored/reversed names 102 pairs vs 93 in Markov-3 REFUTED
8 Semitic triliteral root (morphological) words/skeleton ≈ 1.3, English-like REFUTED
10 Gebofal reordering, 4 geometric models, YHVH/MAD ciphers none beats the null REFUTED

What this says: there is no cipher in the Loagaeth. Not equidistant (ELS), not modular, not acrostic, not neighbour (Soyga-type), not in a third dimension. The ruler is always the same: the real falls within the Markov-3 surrogate’s distribution. Everything that “appears” appears equally in noise with the same phonotactics.

A real numeric finding deserves a note, so as not to hide it: in the number tables of the Heptarchy (not the Loagaeth), the number is “head digit + permuted 2·3·6 block” (z 7.6–9.0; anagram pairs z 13.7) [#28]. It is real, but it is from another Dee document. The Loagaeth does not encode numbers.

7.3 The bridges to the other Enochian systems

The hypothesis dearest to tradition: that the names of the Watchtowers and of Dee’s other systems “live” inside the Loagaeth. We tested it exhaustively, each name as a substring and in pieces, in the whole book and by segment, against composition-matched nulls. The verdict is uniform and negative:

# System Measure Verdict
90 Shem, Goetia, planetary, governors all at Markov-3 expectation; BORNOGO 1× REFUTED
222 Names of the Sigillum Dei Aemeth 2/17 present, null 2.5±0.9, z = −0.54 REFUTED
406 Ars Paulina angels (25, hours+planetary) only ANAEL (1/25) and RAPHAEL (1×), null 1.5 REFUTED
91 “Constellation” of names on stacked faces within both nulls REFUTED
— God names / Kings / Seniors of the Watchtowers (whole and in pieces: BATA, IVAH…) pieces at the null’s frequency REFUTED

There is a structural reason beyond the statistics: Solomonic angels end in -EL (SAMAEL, ANAEL, MICHAEL); in the Loagaeth the suffix -EL is rare (AEL 16×, IEL 5× in the whole book), because the Loagaeth closes in -A [#391, #406]. It is an opposite naming convention — the Loagaeth could not contain those angels even if it wanted to.

Conclusion: the Liber Loagaeth does not contain Dee’s other systems nor the classic magical systems. It is prior and autonomous — the root, not a derivative.

7.4 The bridge to the Calls: kinship, not extraction

A special case, because published researchers claim that the Calls come out of the tables. We tested both forms:

# Claim Measure Verdict
107 Glossed Call words inside the Loagaeth all 26 at Markov-3 expectation REFUTED

128 Every k-th letter gives Call-like text (Laycock) k = 2…12 ≈ shuffled REFUTED

407 “The Calls come from the tables” (Laycock, literal) 147/608 vs null 213 — below chance REFUTED

The Call words are not hidden in the grids — the real text finds fewer than chance (147 vs 213). The Call↔︎table link is language kinship (same phonotactics and lexicon, Ch. 4), not literal extraction nor a page-to-page link. (Keep this for Part III: the traditional “Call opens leaf” map is inherited practice, not a finding of the measure.)

7.8 The 49th leaf and meaning: absences that are findings

Two absences that are not failures, but findings:

  • The 49th leaf — “that is not, was not, and shall not be known” — exists only by report; there is no datum to measure. We record it as a declared absence.
  • The full meaning of each name is not on the page. No internal cipher delivers it (section 7.1); no external source glosses it; our root-names have zero translation anchor [a97]. Dee himself: “Interpret not.” The missing translation was not lost — it was never written. It belongs to the operative plane (Part III), not the statistical one.

What remains standing after the graveyard

After burying more than a hundred hypotheses, what remains standing is exactly what Part I measured: a constructed, consonantal, singable language, woven on a loom of line-and-column, with houses, families, hierarchy and an elemental arc. No cipher, no other system, no number. The Loagaeth is less than tradition fantasized and more than skepticism expected: not a vault of secrets, but a language of names made for the voice. Part III uses it.

PART III — THE OPERATIVE

Chapter 8 — Using the Loagaeth: from measure to rite

This part changes planes. Part I asked “is there objective structure?” and measured. Part III asks “how is it used?” — and operates by sound, correspondence and act, in magic’s own logic. Nothing here deciphers a hidden meaning, because there is no hidden meaning (Part II). What there is is a language of names made for the voice, and a map of where each thing lies. That is enough for a rite.

Statement of planes. This chapter is experimental, derived from analysis — not inherited liturgy nor a guarantee of results. A REFUTED verdict in Part II means “there is no objective cipher”, not “it does not work as practice”. And a distinction this chapter keeps rigid: what is measured (from Part I) and what is tradition (inherited practice, with no support from the measure) are marked separately. I do not mix them.

8.1 What is measured and what is tradition

So as not to sell tradition as science, the explicit separation:

Element of the practice Status
Pronunciation: open syllable, lean on A, penultimate stress, vowel/H ending MEASURED (Ch. 4)
Two registers: speak the Call, sing the name MEASURED (#401)
Vibrate = consonant-identity on the breath of A MEASURED (#402)
Elemental map: body = Earth; deep = dissolution (water/fire) MEASURED (#397)
Name choice by reach/house/zone MEASURED (Ch. 2)
“Call n opens leaf n+1” TRADITION — the textual link was refuted (p = 0.63, #119)
The entity behind a name; the “meaning” of the name OUTSIDE THE MEASURE — sealed meaning

8.2 The two voice registers (measured)

The first operative rule: the Loagaeth has two voices [#401].

  • Speak the Call. The Claves Angelicae are the register of full speech — articulated, directed, syntactic. They open the operation.
  • Sing the name. The table-names are the register of invocation — condensed, consonantal, vibrated. They name the being.

The basic operation is: the Call opens; the name calls.

8.3 The Call ↔︎ leaf link (tradition, with honesty)

Inherited practice (Golden Dawn and the common reading of Dee) associates each Call with a leaf/table. The measure does not support a textual link — the hypothesis “Call n ↔︎ table n+1” gave p = 0.63 [#119], and the Call words are not hidden in the grids (Ch. 7). Therefore:

  • The practitioner following tradition uses Calls 1 and 2 as general and the specific Call of the sub-angle/region, as in the Watchtower system.
  • But know: this is ritual convention, not a correspondence statistics found. What the measure guarantees is the language kinship — Call and name are the same idiom, so reciting them together is linguistically coherent, even though there is no measured “address” linking Call N to leaf N.

The honest statement: one enters by leaf 2 (leaf 1 is sealed, with no Key) and recites Call 1 as the opening — by tradition and language kinship, not because the grid hides the Call.

8.4 Pronunciation and vibration (measured)

Straight from the sound axis (Ch. 4). Dee’s letter-names allow vibration (spelling by each letter’s name):

Letter Name (Dee) Sound
A Un open “ah” (the note)
N Drux “n”
O Med “oh”
H Na aspirated (the breath)
R Don rolled “r”
C Veh “k/ç”

So NOCHA vibrates Drux·Med·Veh·Na·Un. The rules of the chant, all measured:

  1. Open syllables — say each letter; do not swallow vowels (pronounceability z = +6.9).
  2. Lean on the A — the projection note (melody-A z = +5.2). Where there is a strong A, the voice rises and vibrates.
  3. End on the vowel or H — sustain the tone (final-vowel z = +3.2) or release the breath (H final 59%).
  4. Penultimate stress — the Latin cadence (#388).
  5. Pulse every ~3 letters — the A-beat governs the tempo (#398).
  6. Descend the tessitura — bright (A) in the body, dark (U) in the deep.

The consonant is the identity; the vowel is yours. Miss the vowel and it is still the same name; miss the consonant and it is another being [#402]. The operator has freedom of register in the vowel — lengthen it, modulate it, sing it.

8.5 Choosing the name and the house (measured)

Objective criteria (Ch. 2):

  • Reach. NOCHA is the king-name (447 occurrences, 35 leaves, matrix of the D-/AD- house). The natural choice for a first operation of presence and identity.
  • House. House NOCHA (D-/AD-, bright vowel, middle) for mind/word/light; house GETH (L-/X-, dark vowel, edges/deep) for threshold and crossing.
  • Zone. DAXVAR/CHADAX (opening), NOCHA/ACLAXT (middle), CHASTOR (spine), GETH/ALGETH (bottom).

Must I call the “upper” names before the “lower” ones? The nested titles (Ch. 2) suggest hierarchy, but the measure does not prove mandatory precedence — and the test “core born before its titles” fell (23/27 vs 22.7, z 0.19, [#99]). Operatively: the compound name already contains its nucleus; to call it is to call both. The hierarchy is constructive, not a queue protocol.

8.6 The elemental map of the work (measured)

From the elemental arc (Ch. 6), with the honesty of the conflict:

Region Element Work
Leaf 1 — (sealed lexicon) Source of the language; one does not operate by it
Body (2–40) Earth (sign and planet agree, 38/48) Identity, presence, matter, body. From which the beings are called
Seam (26–28) threshold (max chaos) Passage, turning, threshold
Deep (41–48) Water or Fire (rulers conflict) Dissolution and crossing — dissolve (Water) or consume (Fire), per intent. Not fixed identity

The Golden Dawn correspondence of the element (color, incense, direction, planetary day) sets the space — but the core of the operation is the sound of the name in the right region, not the apparatus.

8.7 The evocation sequence (template)

  1. Banishing and consecration of the space. Set the correspondences of the chosen elemental region.
  2. Open by speech. Recite Call 1 (the opening, by tradition) and, if the entity belongs to another region, its specific Call.
  3. Name by song. Vibrate the chosen name in the pronunciation of 8.4 — leaning on the A, pulse every 3, ending on the vowel. Repeat to presence.
  4. Sustain. Keep the region’s vocalic register (bright in the body, dark in the deep).
  5. Dialogue / petition. In the speech register.
  6. License and close. Dismiss, close, banish.

Example — evoking NOCHA (recommended first operation): Leaf 2, opened by Call 1. NOCHA is the king-name of the body (Earth/identity), D-/AD- house, bright vowel. Set an Earth space (sign and planet agree in the body); recite Call 1 as speech; vibrate Drux·Med·Veh·Na·Un (NO-CHA) leaning on the final A, regular pulse; sustain in a bright register. It is the operation of presence and identity — the book’s doorway.

8.8 What the measurement does NOT authorize saying

  • The measure does not deliver the “meaning” of NOCHA or of any name. “Interpret not.”
  • The measure does not prove the rite “works” — that is of another plane. It proves the material has the form of a language of names for the voice, and gives the geography of where each thing lies. The rest is the operator’s.
  • A personal report of contact is journal data, not proof; it is recorded in the ritual journal, not promoted to a conclusion.

Part III ends here. The Apparatus that follows gives the numbered catalog of all findings and the complete methodology, for whoever wishes to redo each measure.

Appendix A — How to redo each measure

Every finding in this book is reproducible bit by bit. The discipline (Ch. 0):

  • Standard-library Python, no external dependencies in the analysis.
  • Fixed seed: 1583 (the year of the Book’s first reception). All randomness starts from it.
  • Null models behind every claim: shuffle, Markov-3 surrogate, controlled permutation/anagram.
  • Explicit verdict: REAL / REFUTED / DESCRIPTIVE / LEAD.
  • Run everything: python src/run_all.py. Each module writes a results/*.json with its statistic and z-score.

The analysis modules (203 results)

The measures live in src/aNNN_*.py, numbered in the order they were made. Main groups:

  • a01–a22 — foundation. Positional grammar, no-doubling rule, line edges, four segments, families (CHASTOR), the two houses, the seam’s diagonal reading, single path in the diamonds, vocalic register, 4–12 letter memory, 2-D rule (horizontal rules).
  • a71–a106 — territories and generator. Line stratification (balanced inventory), names woven into the grid (king-move), territory map by two methods, generative root+affix grammar, 32 predicted new names, super-names (root chains), two lexicon layers, GETH→ACLAX syntax, gematria and cross-system (refuted), entity profiles.
  • a190+ — external names and sound. Watchtower traces (refuted), angels by sub-angle (refuted), the sound axis (pronounceable #386, assonance #387, Latin stress #388, final vowel #391, melody-A #392, A-pulse #398), Menzerath (artifact), two voice registers #401, consonantal identity #402, balanced phonology #403, no positional template #404, grammatical classes by house #405, Ars Paulina absent #406, skip-7 and Laycock refuted #407.

The data

  • Primary source: transcription of the 48 leaves of the Liber Loagaeth (Sloane MS 3189), two sides per leaf; leaf 1 spaced into words (lexicon); the 49th only by report. Holden/Peterson transcription; checked against kondor.de (a copy, 1 letter in 23,712 difference).
  • Alphabet: 21 Enochian letters — A B C D E F G H I L M N O P Q R S T U X Z.
  • Comparison corpus: Calls (Claves Angelicae, Sloane 3191), Watchtowers, 91 governors, Heptarchy, gematria (Liber Scientiae, A True and Faithful Relation).

The interactive screens

The visualizations (in viz/, served locally) accompany the analysis: bilingual catalog, voice of the Loagaeth, occurrence map, structure/loom, dialects, recurrent names, practical guide, Calls↔︎tables, ritual, 3D atlas.

Appendix B — Glossary

  • Null model. A version of the book without the tested structure (shuffled, surrogate or permuted), against which the real is measured.
  • z-score. How many standard deviations the real value lies above/below the null. |z|>3 real; |z|>6 decisive; negative z = anti-structure.
  • Markov-3 surrogate. A text generated respecting the real book’s 3-letter transition probabilities; preserves local phonotactics. The strongest null.
  • Babel principle. A large enough inventory accepts anything by chance; only what beats the null counts.
  • House. A grammatical class of names (house NOCHA D-/AD-; house GETH L-/X-), distinguished by affixes and vocalic register.
  • Family. A set of names with a related consonantal root (NOCHA, GETH, CHASTOR, ANZACH, DAXVAR, ACLAXT, ALGETHA).
  • Minimal pair. Two names identical except for one vowel (pola/pala); proof that the consonant is identity, the vowel is register. 13 vocalic vs 2 consonantal.
  • King-move. The trace (chess king’s step) by which a name is woven into the grid; measures whether the name is stitched or merely resting.
  • Template. The vertical (column) pattern that sustains form without carrying meaning (vertical MI 0.007 bits).
  • Anti-repetition. The line’s tendency to avoid repeating letters (z ≈ −4.5); the line “advances”.
  • Seam (26–28). The threshold band of maximum chaos where the reading migrates to the diagonal.
  • Dissolution arc. The deep (leaves ~41–48), where names vanish, the vowel darkens A→U and elemental identity fractures.
  • Sound axis. The set of properties that make the book singable (pronounceable, assonant, Latin stress, final vowel, melody-A, A-pulse).
  • Two registers. The same language in speech (Calls) and in invocation (table-names).
  • Generative onomasticon. What the Loagaeth is: a book made to generate names of forces.

Appendix C — Closing note and research credit

This book is the honest record of a study that measured the Liber Loagaeth with statistical discipline and kept two planes apart: what the measurement can assert (Parts I–II) and what the practice does with what remained (Part III). The method is the argument: nothing counts without beating the null, and what failed is reported as loudly as what passed — more than a hundred refutations, each with its number.

Any use of the findings, methods, terms or data of this work requires the attribution of the license page:
